item.title: The shear Alfv\'en continuum of optimized stellarators
item.description: arXiv:2611.07182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The shear Alfv\'en continuum has been studied extensively in tokamaks, but its gap structure in modern optimized stellarators has received less attention, despite its importance for energetic-particle confinement in fusion pilot plants. We compute and compare the continua of five reactor-scale stellarator equilibria: two quasi-axisymmetric (QA), two quasi-helically symmetric (QH), and one quasi-isodynamic (QI). We present selective Fourier mode schemes that provide a sufficient resolution of eigenfrequencies within the frequency range of interest. In all five configurations, the widest gap is the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) gap, which is driven by rotating ellipticity. This gap lies in the frequency range of strong resonance with prompt fusion-born alphas in the QA configurations but not in the QH configurations, suggesting that QH configurations may be easier to optimize for alpha confinement. Near-axis theory predicts the HAE(2,$N_{\text{fp}}$) and EAE gap widths well but overestimates the MAE gap widths and the gap widths of the QI configuration. These discrepancies likely arise from interactions between gaps, which depend on the rotational transform profile and are not captured by near-axis theory.
item.dc:creator: Abdullah Hyder, Elizabeth Paul, Alexey Knyazev

item.title: The dielectric tensor for a fully anisotropic regularized Kappa plasma
item.description: arXiv:2611.07220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been known for some decades that the plasma in the Solar System is invariably in a state away from thermal equilibrium. In several plasma environments, be it in the Solar Wind or within planetary magnetospheres, the plasma has been found in a quasi-stationary nonthermal state, with a substantial fraction of its high-energy particles fitting along power-law distributions, instead of the exponential decay of thermal systems. Translating the observations in energy to velocity distribution functions (VDFs), the Kappa plasma model has been employed by the space plasma community, with the (standard) Kappa VDF (SKD) being the preferred choice. However, recent works have called attention to the limitations of the SKD model, proposing as a viable alternative the regularized Kappa VDF (RKD) model, which corrects the deficiencies of the SKD. The RKD model introduces a Gaussian-like dependency on the very high-energy part of the VDF that effectively cut-offs, via a regularization parameter, the Lorentzian profile of the intermediate-energy range. In this work, we employ a generalized RKD that supports anisotropies both in the thermal speed parameters and in the regularization parameters, including as well the possibility of drifts parallel to the magnetic field. This generalized RKD (called the bi-regularized Kappa with drift distribution, bRKd), is employed to derive for the first time the components of the susceptibility tensor for a suprathermal plasma species/population modelled by the bRKd. The tensor components are valid for waves with any propagation angle, frequency range and polarization. During the derivation, new special functions are defined and analyzed, which generalize previous expressions restricted to the parallel propagation limit.
item.dc:creator: Rudi Gaelzer, Horst Fichtner, Dustin Lee Schr\"oder, Marian Lazar, Klaus Scherer

item.title: Suppression of the Laser Hosing Instability in a Parabolic Plasma Channel
item.description: arXiv:2611.07475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analytical stability analysis of the laser hosing instability in a parabolic channel in the weakly relativistic regime. We employ a variational principle approach to derive a set of coupled equations describing laser dynamics in a transversely inhomogeneous plasma. The quadratic Lagrangian formalism is applied to perform a stability analysis and to derive the growth rates for hosing in both long- and short-wavelength regimes. We find that a parabolic channel suppresses the long-wavelength hosing mode completely, for any channel depth, and that the unstable band of the short-wavelength mode is bounded below by a cutoff wavenumber set by the ratio of the channel frequency to the hosing coupling. A steeper channel narrows the unstable band and lowers the short-wavelength growth rate, but cannot stabilize the mode, since the dispersion relation forbids damping identically. The analysis is accompanied by two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, which reproduce the prediction in the nonlinear regime: the long-wavelength mode is absent in a channel, the surviving modulation shortens as the channel steepens, and its amplitude falls with channel depth. Further, our simulation results demonstrate the sensitivity of off-axis laser propagation to the plasma channel and distinguish the hosing instability from laser oscillations due to off-axis laser propagation in a plasma channel.
item.dc:creator: Yash M Jogiya, Vishwa Bandhu Pathak

item.title: Non-axisymmetric MHD equilibria with an arbitrary number of field periods
item.description: arXiv:2611.07672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several closed-form non-axisymmetric magnetic fields with nested toroidal flux surfaces have recently been discovered as exact benchmarks for verifying three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium codes. However, all of these solutions have at most two field periods ($N \le 2$), i.e., identical segments that repeat toroidally. Here, we derive closed-form non-axisymmetric magnetohydrodynamic equilibria for an arbitrary integer number of field periods $N \geq 1$. The equilibria have non-constant pressure and closed magnetic field lines with either zero rotational transform ($\iota = 0$) for $N \geq 1$ or integer rotational transform ($\iota = \pm N$) for $N \ge 3$. For the reflection-symmetric $\iota = 0$ equilibria, we also construct a matched exterior vacuum field with continuous magnetic field across the plasma boundary, providing a benchmark for free-boundary equilibrium codes.
item.dc:creator: Opal Issan, Lucas Jos\'e, Matt Landreman, Jonathan Citrin, Brendan Tracey

item.title: Edge turbulence controlled by topologically self-optimized fluxes in fusion devices
item.description: arXiv:2603.28633v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The magnetic field topology undergoes a drastic transition near the separatrix in magnetic confinement fusion devices, inducing topological chaos. This phenomenon is investigated across tokamaks, stellarators, and the RFX-mod reversed-field pinch. Within this boundary region, self-optimized fluxes of shear-generated magnetic and cross-helicity, together with the ensemble-averaged magnetic moment, are hypothesized to govern plasma stability, self-organization, and transport. By treating the averaged magnetic moment as an active scalar and using the Fokker-Planck equation to reconcile kinetic and fluid descriptions, this study couples its dynamics with a novel multichannel, self-optimized helicity cascade loop. The derived spectral laws for the floating potential and ion saturation current agree with measurements from numerous experiments. Distributed chaos theory quantifies the randomness of the observed states, revealing that a narrow layer at the separatrix suppresses strong core randomness, transforming it into distributed chaos in the scrape-off layer. A constrained variational principle for active control has also been considered. Tuning Lagrangian multipliers via helicity injection drives the system toward an attractor state that stabilizes the separatrix shear layer, suppresses edge-localized modes, and spreads the heat load, using magnetic reconnection as a nonlinear solver. This framework circumvents conventional diffusive limitations, providing an analytical foundation to model heat-load patterns and stochastic ripple loss in next-step devices.
item.dc:creator: A. Bershadskii

item.title: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.07102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sample-based quantum subspace methods construct a small subspace from measured basis states and solve the target problem classically within it. We study these methods for heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where the anisotropy $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp$ reaches $10^8$ to $10^{10}$. We prove two results for the energy-norm Galerkin solution. First, if the measurement basis is aligned with the flux surfaces and the subspace contains the poloidal-mode-zero block, the error is bounded by $\|r_0\|_{L^+}(\chi_\parallel-\chi_\perp)^{-1/2}$, where the numerator does not depend on $\chi_\parallel$. The bound is sharp, so the accuracy improves as the anisotropy grows. Second, in the computational basis, a subspace that misses a single node of a flux surface suppresses the flux-function component there as $\chi_\parallel^{-1/2}$, which gives an error floor when the limiting solution is nonzero on that surface. We verify both results on a shaped cross-section and on a KSTAR-like Miller equilibrium with ten qubits. At $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp=10^9$, the computational basis gives an error of order unity for every shot budget, whereas a quantum Fourier transform on the poloidal register gives $1.3\times10^{-5}$. The same barrier limits sample-based quantum diagonalization. The aligned measurement needs no time evolution, so the circuit is only state preparation and a five-qubit quantum Fourier transform. On a ten-qubit superconducting processor, the aligned basis gives a median error of $7.0\times10^{-6}$ with 768 shots, whereas the computational basis gives errors above 0.94 up to $1.2\times10^4$ shots. A trapped-ion processor shows the same behavior.
item.dc:creator: Doyeol (David), Ahn (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Newport Beach, California, USA)

item.title: A physics-based adaptive low-rank method for 6D Vlasov simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.07107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank $r$ objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Cassini, Lukas Einkemmer

item.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.07121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $\zeta(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $\Delta_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $\kappa_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $\kappa_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-\chi r$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $\chi$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Svitlana Mayboroda, Camillo de Lellis, David N. Spergel, Max Engelstein

item.title: Winding-Pack Quench Simulation of Stellarator Coils: Hydraulic Field-Network Coupling and Transverse Heat Conduction in OPENSC$^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quench propagation in cable-in-conduit conductors is thermo-hydraulically driven, yet existing 1D models treat a conductor as one straight adiabatic cable with prescribed pressure and mass-flow boundaries, so secondary quenches and flow redistribution between windings cannot be resolved. We extend the open-source code OPENSC$^2$ with transverse heat conduction between turns, a 3D field resolving the current-sharing temperature, induced losses, and a lumped hydraulic network coupled to the conductors by a mass-flow formulation. Validated against the 2006 W7-X coil tests, it predicts the quench site, cuts the outlet-temperature error from 55 K to 12 K, and reproduces the neighboring windings' heating as flow reversal through the coil inlet.
item.dc:creator: Laura A. M. D'Angelo, Felix Warmer

item.title: Exact Solution of the Direct and Inverse Quasi-stationary Dynamo Problem in the Expanding Plasma Ball
item.description: arXiv:2607.12194v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that differential equation of the quasi-stationary dynamo effect (i.e., generation of the electric fields and currents) in a uniformly-expanding plasma ball with strongly anisotropic conductivity possesses the unique mathematical property: namely, the spectrum of its eigenvalues is universal and independent of physical parameters of the medium. As a result, it becomes possible to introduce a special set of eigenfunctions - which we called the generalized spherical functions - that can be used to solve the dynamo problem in exactly the same way as ordinary spherical functions are used to solve the Laplace equation. The corresponding exact solutions should be especially valuable for treating the inverse dynamo problem, i.e., determination of the plasma parameters from the experimentally measured electric fields and currents.
item.dc:creator: Yurii V. Dumin

item.title: Drift wave turbulence and transport analysis of hot ion L-mode plasma with fishbone instability on HL-3 tokamak
item.description: arXiv:2610.35072v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An integrated analysis of the HL-3 hot-ion L-mode (shot \#11972, $T_i/T_e\approx3$, $T_i(0)\approx9.8$\,keV) establishes the cross-scale coupling by which a single $m=1,n=1$ fishbone mode governs both toroidal rotation and ion-scale drift-wave turbulence. Multi-diagnostic measurements, OMFIT integrated modeling, and TGLF quasilinear simulations show that a steep fast-ion pressure gradient under 2.5\,MW co-injected NBI excites the fishbone. Its outward redistribution of resonant fast ions decouples the NBI torque, and the sawtooth crash it triggers collapses the rotation from above $100$ to $60$\,krad/s. The same fast ions that drive the fishbone also stabilize ion-scale ITG/TEM turbulence, so their redistribution removes the ITG stabilization carried by the high temperature ratio, fast-ion dilution, and $E\times B$ shear, and erodes the internal transport barrier. Two-dimensional flux and one-dimensional eigenvalue scans confirm that the high temperature ratio and the fast-ion population together suppress particle, energy, and momentum transport. These findings close one cross-scale coupling loop spanning MHD, fast-ion transport and microturbulence, in which one mode drives both momentum balance and turbulence stability. The results offer a predictive framework for fast-ion confinement and rotation sustainment in the upcoming deuterium tritium phase, and for burning plasmas where alpha particles likewise drive MHD activity and damp turbulence.
item.dc:creator: Y. K. Shu, W. Chen, Z. J. Li, S. Xu, Y. F. Liu, B. L. Hao, Z. Wang, D. L. Yu, S. S. Yang, W. Y. Zhai, X. L. Zhu, P. W. Shi, X. L. Xu, T. Wu, Z. B. Shi, HL-3 Team

item.title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
item.description: arXiv:2611.04906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.
item.dc:creator: R Datta, C Clauser, G Hu, A Braun, N Ferraro, R Sweeney, R A Tinguely

item.title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
item.description: arXiv:2611.06045v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa. Using in situ orientation-resolved single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we observe discrete Bragg spots whose spacings and angular relationships are reproduced by a common orientation matrix within each indexed BC8 reflection group, providing constraints beyond powder peak matching. Our single-crystal formation strategy and direct diffraction evidence resolve the decades-long quest for a post-diamond carbon structure, demonstrating how dynamic loading pathways can make predicted high-pressure phases experimentally accessible.
item.dc:creator: Liang Sun, Bo Chen, Zhiyu He, Pin Yang, Zanyang Guan, Guo Jia, Fan Zhang, Yi Yang, Bo Xu, Pei Guo, Yonggang Liu, Wei Fan, Tao Xi, Yulong Li, Lingbiao Meng, Wei Kang, Zhiyong Xie, Yuqiong Tu, Cheng Ji, Xiuguang Huang, Zhongjing Chen, Ji Yan, Jiamin Yang, Wenge Yang, Toshimori Sekine, Zongqing Zhao, Jiayu Dai, Ho-Kwang Mao
